name_note: GTDB g__Aquipseudomonas is a recently separated Pseudomonadaceae genus whose members, including Pseudomonas viridiflava and Pseudomonas monteilii, still carry Pseudomonas names in NCBI.

sentences.text: Aquipseudomonas is one of several genera recently separated from the broad genus Pseudomonas, which phylogenomic work showed to be a diverse assemblage without a single common evolutionary history.
Members such as Aquipseudomonas alcaligenes have been recovered from aquatic environments, for example the filter and gravel of a home aquarium.
Pseudomonas viridiflava was identified, with Pseudomonas mediterranea, as a causal agent of tomato pith necrosis in Al Taif, Saudi Arabia, and pathogenicity assays showed it caused severe necrosis.
A case report described Pseudomonas monteilii sepsis in a 55-year-old man immediately after insertable cardiac monitor implantation, with the organism identified in blood culture.
